newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX starts lower after technical hitch.
newsitem.headline: German DAX starts lower after technical hitch.

text.p: German shares on Thursday opened weaker after the 101-point fall in the Dow Jones index on Tuesday but dealers said they did not expect any further strong declines amid particularly weak trading volumes.
By late morning, the DAX index of 30 leading German shares stood 46.50 points, or 1.61 percent, lower at 2,842.19.

Earlier, the IBIS electronic share dealing system had been delayed by over an hour due to technical problems, but dealers said the lack of any serious trading volumes meant the interruption had had little impact on share values.
"The delay was of little importance because there is scarcely anybody here," one dealer said.
March DAX futures traded 56.0 points down at 2,848.5 as German debt futures were also taken lower by a fall in U.S. Treasuries.
Traders said the slight recovery of the dollar to around 1.547 marks from some the low of some 1.536 marks reached on January 31, was meanwhile acting as a support for German shares.
Individual share losers included banks Bayerische Hypo and Commerzbank, down 1.20 marks to 45.35 and 75 pfennigs to 38.35 respectively, but with volumes relatively low in both cases.
Insurer Allianz dipped 60 marks to 2,740, while chemical and auto stocks all fell with the trend.
